questiontext.text:
Background Notes:

  • In a triangle, each side is opposite an angle: side a opposite ∠A, side b opposite ∠B, side c opposite ∠C.
  • The Sine Rule helps us find missing sides or angles: \[ \frac{a}{\sin A} = \frac{b}{\sin B} = \frac{c}{\sin C} \]
  • We will use this rule to find the missing side.

Step-by-Step Guide:

  1. First, write down what is given: two angles and one side.
  2. Identify the side and angle pairs (side a with ∠A, side b with ∠B).
  3. Apply the sine rule: \[ \frac{a}{\sin A} = \frac{b}{\sin B} \]
  4. Rearrange: \[ b = \frac{a \cdot \sin B}{\sin A} \]

Now try this problem:

In the triangle below:

  • ∠A = {@A@}°
  • ∠B = {@B@}°
  • ∠C = {@C@}°
  • Side a = {@a@} units (opposite ∠A)

Use the Sine Rule to find the length of side \(b\) (opposite ∠B).

Give your answer correct to 3 decimal places.

Side \( b = \) [[input:ans1]] units

[[validation:ans1]][[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution

We are given:

  • ∠A = {@A@}°
  • ∠B = {@B@}°
  • ∠C = {@C@}°
  • Side a = {@a@} units (opposite ∠A)

We want to find side \( b \), which is opposite ∠B.

Step 1: Recall the Sine Rule: \( \displaystyle \frac{a}{\sin A} = \frac{b}{\sin B} = \frac{c}{\sin C} \)

Step 2: Use only the pairs involving \(a\) and \(b\): \(\displaystyle \frac{a}{\sin A} = \frac{b}{\sin B} \)

Step 3: Rearrange to make \(b\) the subject: \(\displaystyle b = \frac{a \cdot \sin B}{\sin A} \)

Step 4: Substitute the known values: \( \displaystyle b = \frac{{@a@} \cdot \sin({@B@}°)}{\sin({@A@}°)} \)

Step 5: Calculate: \( b = {@ta@} \text{ units} \) (correct to 3 Decimal places)
